topic: MBA Reports: Porter's, SWOT & Financial Ratios

copy.facebook:
If you’re currently working on an MBA strategic management report, let’s talk about that '2:2 trap' I keep seeing. 

Too many students treat SWOT and Porter’s Five Forces as isolated tasks. In the real world—and in top-tier grading rubrics—it’s all about the synthesis. If you aren't cross-analyzing your internal VRIO core competencies against external macro-risks, you’re missing the point of the assignment. 

Here is how to pivot:

• Move beyond listing: Always justify your strategic recommendations with financial data like ROIC or EBITDA.
• Implementation: Don't just give advice; provide a budgeted, realistic roadmap.
• Integration: Ensure every framework feeds into the next. 

I know these reports are heavy on the word count and even heavier on the analysis. If you feel like you’re hitting a wall, reach out. We can walk through your draft and make sure your logic holds up under pressure.
